mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not lead to tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS 3-month % change > 2% does not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher costs for businesses, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 5% does not lead to wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO > 12-month MA does not correlate with economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not lead to reduced borrowing costs.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market with strong job growth, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher costs for businesses, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong job growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not lead to wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1% signals increased borrowing costs, which reduces corporate investment and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 1% does not lead to reduced corporate investment.
